1. Prayer in the present writ petition, filed under Article 226/227 of the Constitution of India is for release of land under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.
Challenge has also been raised to the order dated 08.09.2017 (Annexure P-10) passed by the authorities.

2. Respondent No.3-the Administrator, HUDA, while passing the said order, in compliance of the earlier directions issued by this Court in CWP-14650-2015 filed by the petitioner, took into consideration the representation which had been sought to be decided wherein the petitioner had claimed that he was owner of 2 kanals of land situated within the revenue estate of Village Tigra,
Tehsil & District Gurugram and had not received compensation for the land and was in physical possession of the land and constructed a house on it.

The said respondent, resultantly, came to the conclusion that the land falling in Rect. No.21 Killa No.6/1 (2-0) 1 of 13 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120431-DB CWP-23810-2017 share holder 1 Kanal, Rect. No.22, Killa No.10 (4-0)
had been notified for the development of residential, commercial and institutional Sector-57, as per the notification dated 24.08.2000 (Annexure P-1) wherein 546.24 acres of land was sought to be Jagdish Chand vs State Of Haryana And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53027828/
1 acquired for Villages Wazirabad, Tigra, badshapur, Ghata, Ghasola, Nangli, Umerpur and Samaspur, Tehsil & District Gurugram.

The houses in Khasras No.20//10 min(1-12) were left out under Section 5-A of the Right to Fair Compensation & Transperancy in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation & Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, the '2013 Act') and vested with the Government and rest of the khasras numbers along with land measuring 505.65 acres were notified under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 issued on 22.08.2001 (Annexure P-2).

sentences.text: The land of Village Tigra measuring 172.52 acres was acquired vide award No.10 dated 21.07.2003 (Annexure P-3) and possession had been handed-over to HUDA vide rapat No.583 of even date.
The applicant's father, Charan Singh was stated to be a Dholidar in half share of the plots.

The utility of the land was for the purposes of setting up 10 number of plots in 10 marla category and two No.10 meter wide internal road and as per the plan, plot Nos.682EP, 682G, 682L, 682I, 682K, 682L, 682M, 682N which had already been allotted.

3. It is thus the stand of the State that out of Khasra Nos.20//10 min (1-12) was left out of the original 4 kanals in view of the recommendations of the constituted Zonal Committee having approved by the competent authority who had not found merit in the claim for lapsing and if there was any structure on the acquired land, the department would make payment of it and demolish the same and if there was no structure, possession was to be delivered at a later stage.

The occupation was thus 2 of 13 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120431-DB CWP-23810-2017 held to be unauthorized, illegal on account of physical possession having been taken and having the right as a Dholidar
, it was held that he had no right of ownership and therefore, could not claim right on the land and thus, could only claim compensation.

The acquisition proceedings having attained finality,
keeping in mind the recommendations of the constituted Joint Site Inspection Committees, the claim of lapsing of the acquisition was rejected which led to filing of the present writ petition.
Resultantly, the petitioner had approached this Court on the plea that compensation as required per law was not paid to the petitioner.
4. The writ petition had initially been disposed of along with bunch of cases, lead case being CWP-13425-2015 titled Vijay Pal and others Vs. State of Haryana & others, decided on 29.01.2018.

The said judgment having been set aside by the Apex Court in CA-4804/-2024 on 08.04.2024 and the matter has been sent back for fresh consideration, in the light of the judgment in Indore Development Authority Vs. Manoharlal &
others, AIR 2020 SC 1496, keeping all the contentions open.

It was further averred that the petitioner was doing dairy business 3 of 13 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120431-DB CWP-23810-2017 on the land and was never put to notice to vacate the physical possession and claim was made that he had been declared Dholidar as per order dated 14.11.2011 passed by the Reference Court and therefore, had claimed the compensation on that account.

sentences.text: In such circumstances, counsel for the petitioner has argued that objection having been filed under Section 5-A of the 1894 Act, the issue of discrimination would arise that he was entitled for release as the house of the petitioner was also adjoining Village Tigra.
Similarly, reference was also made to another set of landowners, namely, Tej Ram, Madan Lal, Daya Chand and Pirthi, sons of Nathu Ram.

7. The State, in its reply, appended the objections filed under Section 5-A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 dated 21.09.2000 (Annexure R-1) wherein objection was taken that the applicant was co- owner of land measuring 15 kanals 11 marlas to the extent of half share.

Plea was taken that Killa No.10 Khasra No.22 wherein the petitioner had constructed 2 tin sheds, verandah and chabutra and it was bounded by four-walls and there existed a iron gate in Killa No.6/1 constructed on the boundary wall and tin-shed and the remaining land was residential and used for Samadhi in Killa No.6/2 of Swami Silak Ram and touching the village and therefore, keeping in view the vicinity of the abadi which was stated to be close-by, the exemption from acquisition had been sought.
It is as per the record that the release of the residential portion in Khasra No.21//6/2 had been recommended and the rest of the land had been recommended for acquisition.
The release was therefore of class-B residential house along with proportionate open space.
The report was 4 of 13 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120431-DB CWP-23810-2017 attached of the JSIC as Annexure R-2.

Relevant portion of the report wherein land had been recommended for release reads as under:
 "Objection No. Name of Objector Village  3 Jagdish s/o Charan Singh Tigra In Khasra No.22//10 exist one B class residential house- 50'x30'.

Entire area of 6/2 is recommended to be released."
8.

It is thus the stand of the State that the acquisition was made by passing the award on 21.07.2003 for land measuring 172.25 acres out of the land measuring 189.93 acres notified under Section 4 of the Act and reduced down to 171.11 acres for Village Tigra.
The need for the land had already been mentioned in the speaking order (Annexure P-10) which is subject matter of challenge.
The State objected on the ground of dismissal of the first round of litigation in CWP-18268-2002, which was done on 21.04.2007 (Annexure R-6).

It has further been averred that the petitioner had filed reference petition under Sections 18 & 30 bearing LAC Case No.180 of 26.05.2005 and the same was allowed in his favour by the Reference Court on 23.02.2010 (Annexure R-8) and the value of the land was assessed @ Rs.888/- per sq.yard.

The amount was further got enhanced by filing RFA-5095-2010 titled Jagdish Vs. Land Acquisition Collector & others, and compensation was fixed @ Rs.1216/- per sq.yard on 10.12.2015 (Annexure R-9) by a Learned Single Judge of this Court.

sentences.text:
The relevant portion reads as under:
"34.
It is well settled that a prerogative remedy is not a matter of course.
In exercising extraordinary power, therefore, a Writ Court will indeed bear in mind the conduct of the party who is invoking such jurisdiction.
If the applicant does not disclose full facts or suppresses relevant materials or is otherwise guilty of misleading the Court, the Court may dismiss the action without adjudicating the matter.
The rule has been evolved in larger public interest to deter unscrupulous litigants from abusing the process of Court by deceiving it.
The very basis of the writ jurisdiction rests in disclosure of true, complete and correct facts.
If the material facts are not candidly stated or are suppressed or are distorted, the very functioning of the writ courts would become impossible."

Issue of discrimination :
10. The issue of lapsing already stands decided against the petitioner as on an earlier occasion the writ petition having been allowed, the same has now been set aside and Jagdish Chand vs State Of Haryana And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53027828/

sentences.text: the matter having been sent to be decided on merits by the Apex Court.

The only issue which arises is whether if there is any plea of discrimination which had been adequately met by the State, as noticed, that specific plea was regarding 7 of 13 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120431-DB CWP-23810-2017 discrimination on release for similarly situated persons.
The petitioner in his writ petition did not plead before this Court that he had already been given the benefit of release of the land on the constructed portion having been pleaded by the State.

On an earlier occasion, the co-sharers with whom the petitioner had preferred petitions under Sections 18 and 30 of the Act, namely, Jiwan Lal, Mehar Chand, Indraj, Bhoop Singh had filed CWP-16946-2001, which was prior to the award being passed and it was their specific case for release on the ground that there was construction at that point of time regarding the land falling in Khasra No.21, Killa No.6/1, 6//2, 22//10, 24//18/1 and 21//15.

Finding was recorded while deciding the said petitions along with others that the constructed portion had already been left out of the acquisition and there was scattered C-class construction and the issue of illegality and discrimination had been rejected.

Relevant portion of the order reads as under:
"In CWP Nos.16946 of 2001, since the constructed portion has already been left from acquisition and the remaining portion which was vacant or having scattered 'C' class construction, has been acquired, we do not find any illegality or discrimination in the acquisition of the land of the petitioners."
11.

At the initial stage, before the passing of the order, there was a specific contention raised that there was construction and the Division Bench, at that point of time, had given permission to place photographic evidence as proof of A-Class construction vide orders dated 16.11.2002 and 14.01.2003 and it is only thereafter, the writ petition had been dismissed on 24.04.2007.
It is thus apparent that petitioner has continuously been approaching this Court time and again frustrating the purpose of planned land development which the State is seeking to achieve 8 of 13

and after having got the necessary release of the constructed portion and also having successfully agitated for his grievances regarding compensation for the balance land which stands finalized acquired uptill the Apex Court

. Reference regarding the release of land, as mentioned in favour of other landowners, is without any basis, as the release order was appended in CWP-7855-2017 titled Raj Kumar & others Vs. State of Haryana & others.

sentences.text: It is to be noticed that thereafter, after the award was passed on 21.07.2003, the petitioner preferred his remedy under Sections 18 & 30 of the Act by filing LAC-180-2005 along with his co-sharers, Jiwan Lal Mehar Chand, Indrraj and Bhoop Singh sons of Rattan Lal son of Bihari 9 of 13 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120431-DB CWP-23810-2017 whereas he is son of Charan Singh son of Bihari.

The issue in dispute was that being close to village abadi of land falling in Rect.
No.21, 22, 24 and to the extent of ownership of half share in which he was arrayed as petitioner No.5.

Specific plea was raised that they had constructed very big construction in Rectange No.21, 22 & 24 by spending Rs.50 lakhs and one Jai Lal was arrayed as respondent in the said reference petition as he was claiming acquisition of land being owner and wanting to receive compensation.
The claim was made on the ground that there was a Gift in favour of the petitioner's predecessor-in-interest.
Reference was also made to the earlier writ filed bearing CWP-16946-2000 that they had raised challenge in that case to the notification.

In the reference petition decided along with the bunch of cases by the Reference Court on 23.02.2010 (Annexure R-8), Reference Court has not awarded compensation since there was no structure standing on the land in LAC-180-2005.
The resultant finding was that no evidence was led on the said issue and neither the issue was pressed during the course of arguments.

Relevant observations read as under:
"Additional Issue framed in L.A.case nos.21 of 2005, 31 of 2005, 51 of 2006, 81 of 2005, 87 of 2005, 93 of 2005, 103 of 2005, 178 of 2005, 180 of 2005, 183 of 2005,
186 of 2005, 190 of 2005, 195 of 2005, 199 of 2005, 201 of 2005, 435 of 2004, 538 of 2004 and 554 of 2004:
28.
The onus to prove this issue was on the petitioners that there existed any super structure on the acquired land.
No evidence has been led on this issue nor this issue was pressed during the course of arguments.
Therefore, the issue stands decided against the petitioners."

13. It is, thus, crystal clear that the claim on the ground of releasing out the constructed portion was not only repelled, firstly, in the 10 of 13 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120431-DB CWP-23810-2017 case of co-sharers in CWP-16946-2001 on 14.11.2003 by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court but also by the Reference Court while deciding the reference petition on 23.02.2010, as noted above.
The claim is also only on the right of not being the owner of the property in any manner but being a Dholidar.

Apparently, a separate petition was also filed bearing LAC-50-2006 decided on 14.11.2011 (Annexure P-11) in which petitioner along with other co-sharers, in which he was arrayed as petitioner No.5, filed another petition under Sections 18 & 30 against Jai Dayal.

The said case was also decided along with LAC Case No.5 of 2005 titled Guru Prasad & others Vs. LAC &
others in which Charan Singh son of Bihari (deceased) through his LRs, Jagdish Chand has been arrayed as respondent No.4 wherein while noticing that the market value of the land had been fixed by this Court at Rs.1216/- per sq.yard, the claimants were held entitled for compensation in respect of Khasra No.21 measuring 6 kanals falling in Killa No.18/2(6-0).

sentences.text: Even otherwise, the Act itself came into force on 04.03.2011 and petitioner cannot get any benefit retrospectively and also having been agitating for their right of compensation before the Court of competent jurisdiction and therefore, cannot now claim that the land is not liable to be acquired.

Reliance can be placed upon the observations made in Indore Development Authority ( s u p r a ) r e g a r d i n g t h e c o n s e q u e n c e s o f p e r s u i n g 1 1 o f 1 3 N e u t r a l C i t a t i o n No:=2024:PHHC:120431-DB CWP-23810-2017 the claim for higher compensation in Court.

Relevant portion of the judgment reads as under:
"224.
Thus, in our opinion, the word "paid" used in Section 24(2) does not include within its meaning the word "deposited", which has been used in the proviso to Section 24(2).

Section 31 of the Act of 1894, deals with the deposit as envisaged in Section 31(2) on being 'prevented' from making the payment even if the amount has been deposited in the treasury under the Rules framed under Section 55 or under the Standing Orders, that would carry the interest as envisaged under Section 34, but acquisition would not lapse on such deposit being made in the treasury.
In case amount has been tendered and the landowner has refused to receive it, it cannot be said that the liability arising from non-payment of the amount is that of lapse of acquisition.
Interest would follow in such a case also due to non-deposit of the amount.

Equally, when the landowner does not accept the amount, but seeks a reference for higher compensation, there can be no question of such individual stating that he was not paid the amount (he was determined to be entitled to by the collector).
In such case, the landowner would be entitled to the compensation determined by the Reference Court."

Viability and essentiality of acquired land :
14. The issue of discrimination cannot be raised as the constructed portion has already been released.
The claim for release of the land on the ground of construction having been raised

has already been repelled and even the petitioner failed to lead any evidence before the Reference Court and therefore, now cannot claim any such benefit in writ jurisdiction without challenging the findings of the Reference Court.

The reasoning that the land is required for the purpose of plots and for construction of roads has been confirmed from the site-plan placed on record by the State,
showing the location of the land in question 12 of 13 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120431-DB CWP-23810-2017 (Annexure R-3) and the administrative authorities have already adjudicated on the said issue and passed a speaking order on 21.07.2003 and no fault can be found in the same.

15. The above cumulative discussion would go on to show that this is the fourth round of litigation in the Writ Court by the petitioner and his co-sharers, admittedly, CWP-7612-2022 is also still pending.

In the said writ petition, petitioner has taken the plea that his entire construction in Khasra No.22//10(5-12) had been released from acquisition proceedings as per the stand of the Jagdish Chand vs State Of Haryana And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53027828/
7

entities.text: Jagdish Chand vs State Of Haryana And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: State filed in CWP-16946-2001 and thus, apparently, had relied upon the fact that his co-sharers had filed the said proceedings which is prior to the award passed.

Strangely enough, the petitioner is absolutely silent in regarding the filing of the said petition and the same has only been put-forth by the State and therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that an effort has been made to continue to get interim orders by way of filing repeated litigation and the mala-fide is but apparent.

The present writ petition, thus, deserves to be dismissed, necessarily with costs of Rs.25,000/-, to be deposited with the Blind School, Sector 26, Chandigarh within 2 months, failing which, Collector,
Gurugram shall recover the same as arrears of Land Revenue.
15. Writ petition stands dismissed, accordingly, with the above- said direction.
(G.S. SANDHAWALIA)

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The rule has been evolved in larger public interest to deter unscrupulous litigants from abusing the process of Court by deceiving it.
The very basis of the writ jurisdiction rests in disclosure of true, complete and correct facts.
The petitioner in his writ petition did not plead before this Court that he had already been given the benefit of release of the land on the constructed portion having been pleaded by the State.
. Reference regarding the release of land, as mentioned in favour of other landowners, is without any basis, as the release order was appended in CWP-7855-2017 titled Raj Kumar & others Vs. State of Haryana & others.
The claim is also only on the right of not being the owner of the property in any manner but being a Dholidar.
The entitlement was, thus,
prospective, limited to the extent to receive compensation on the ground of being in possession and no declaration had been given under the Haryana Dholidar, Butimar, Bhondedar and Muqararidar Jagdish Chand vs State Of Haryana And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53027828/
6 (Vesting of Proprietary Rights) Act, 2010 that they were owners and thus, would be entitled for release.
Even otherwise, the Act itself came into force on 04.03.2011 and petitioner cannot get any benefit retrospectively and also having been agitating for their right of compensation before the Court of competent jurisdiction and therefore, cannot now claim that the land is not liable to be acquired.
The claim for release of the land on the ground of construction having been raised
has already been repelled and even the petitioner failed to lead any evidence before the Reference Court and therefore, now cannot claim any such benefit in writ jurisdiction without challenging the findings of the Reference Court.
The reasoning that the land is required for the purpose of plots and for construction of roads has been confirmed from the site-plan placed on record by the State,
showing the location of the land in question 12 of 13 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120431-DB CWP-23810-2017 (Annexure R-3) and the administrative authorities have already adjudicated on the said issue and passed a speaking order on 21.07.2003 and no fault can be found in the same.
In the said writ petition, petitioner has taken the plea that his entire construction in Khasra No.22//10(5-12) had been released from acquisition proceedings as per the stand of the Jagdish Chand vs State Of Haryana And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53027828/
7
Strangely enough, the petitioner is absolutely silent in regarding the filing of the said petition and the same has only been put-forth by the State and therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that an effort has been made to continue to get interim orders by way of filing repeated litigation and the mala-fide is but apparent.
opennyai_summary.issue: The only issue which arises is whether if there is any plea of discrimination which had been adequately met by the State, as noticed, that specific plea was regarding 7 of 13 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120431-DB CWP-23810-2017 discrimination on release for similarly situated persons.

15. Writ petition stands dismissed, accordingly, with the above- said direction.
